title: Case 1: Administration of Scheduled & Tribal Areas (Fifth & Sixth Schedules) (Article 244 • Writ Petition)
legalTheme: Part X: The Scheduled and Tribal Areas • Article 244
factualMatrix: Before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32), an aggrieved petitioner challenged an impugned executive notification and enforcement order issued by the Union Ministry / Central Authority under Article 244 (Administration of Scheduled & Tribal Areas (Fifth & Sixth Schedules)) of Part X (The Scheduled and Tribal Areas). Relying on the core guarantee that Establishes a distinctive asymmetric constitutional regime for the governance of indigenous tribal communities: Clause (1) applies the Fifth Schedule to Scheduled Areas in 10 mainland States, empowering the Governor to shield tribals from general laws;... and citing Samatha v. 3. How does Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
statutoryApplicability: Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997)
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 244 (Part X).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 244): Establishes a distinctive asymmetric constitutional regime for the governance of indigenous tribal communities: Clause (1) applies the Fifth Schedule to Scheduled Areas in 10 mainland States, empowering the Governor to shield tribals from general laws;... factualMatrix: In a Constitutional Reference instituted before the Constitution Bench (Article 145(3)), the Court examined whether an disciplinary / disqualification directive by the State Government Department complied with Article 244A (Formation of an Autonomous State Comprising Tribal Areas in Assam). Grounded in Part X (The Scheduled and Tribal Areas), where Inserted by the 22nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1969: Empowers Parliament by law to form an autonomous State within the State of Assam comprising certain tribal areas, and to create a local Legislature or Council of Ministers therefor., the parties contested the binding effect of Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997) on the factual record.
framingQuestions: 1. Whether the Constitutional Reference before the Constitution Bench (Article 145(3)) is maintainable under Article 244A?
2. Does the State Government Department's disciplinary / disqualification directive conform to Article 244A (Formation of an Autonomous State Comprising Tribal Areas in Assam)?
3. How does Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
statutoryApplicability: Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997)
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Constitutional Reference before the Constitution Bench (Article 145(3)) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 244A (Part X).

SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 244A): Inserted by the 22nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1969: Empowers Parliament by law to form an autonomous State within the State of Assam comprising certain tribal areas, and to create a local Legislature or Council of Ministers therefor.
